name: 27th Amendment
kicker: Delays congressional pay changes until after an election · Ratified 1992
briefing: The 27th Amendment says that if Congress changes its own pay, the change cannot take effect until after the next election for the House of Representatives. James Madison proposed it in 1789, but it sat unratified for almost two centuries. Then in 1982, a University of Texas student named Gregory Watson wrote a paper about it, got a C, and started a letter-writing campaign. It was finally ratified in 1992, about 202 years after Congress first proposed it.
answerHtml: Twenty-seventh Amendment (or 27th Amendment or Amendment XXVII; accept Congressional Compensation Amendment)
reject: district of columbia voting rights amendment

tossups.p: In 1982, a University of Texas student named Gregory Watson wrote a paper arguing that this amendment, which Congress had proposed almost two centuries earlier, could still be ratified. He got a C on the paper and then launched a letter-writing campaign to state lawmakers.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment, ratified in 1992, which delays changes in congressional pay until after the next House election.

tossups.p: When James Madison introduced his proposed amendments in the House in June 1789, he included this one. It was second on the list of twelve that Congress sent to the states that September, just ahead of the amendment protecting freedom of speech.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment about congressional pay, which was finally ratified in 1992.

tossups.p: The word “varying” in this amendment means it covers pay cuts as well as raises. Its single sentence was first proposed by James Madison, who also drafted the amendments that became the Bill of Rights.
tossups.r: It says such a change cannot “take effect, until an election of Representatives shall have intervened.” For 10 points, name this amendment ratified in 1992.

tossups.p: In 1873, Ohio’s legislature approved this long-forgotten amendment to protest the “Salary Grab Act,” under which members of Congress had given themselves a raise along with back pay for the previous two years.
tossups.r: More than a century later, it was finally ratified. For 10 points, name this amendment that delays congressional pay changes until after the next House election.

tossups.p: In 1978, Wyoming’s legislature approved this amendment to protest a congressional pay raise, more than a century after Ohio had done the same thing for the same reason. Four years later, a college student began a national campaign for it.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment, first proposed by James Madison, that was ratified in 1992.

tossups.p: No other amendment took nearly as long to ratify as this one, which became part of the Constitution about 202 years after Congress sent it to the states. Because it was proposed long before Congress began setting deadlines for ratification, it never expired.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment, ratified in 1992, that deals with pay raises for members of Congress.

tossups.p: In May 1992, the Archivist of the United States, Don W. Wilson, certified this amendment as ratified, and both houses of Congress then passed resolutions, by lopsided votes, agreeing that it was valid.
tossups.r: A college student’s letter-writing campaign had revived it. For 10 points, name this amendment that delays any congressional pay raise until after the next House election.

tossups.p: Questions about whether this amendment had taken too long to ratify recalled the 1939 case _Coleman v. Miller_, in which the Supreme Court said that Congress, not the courts, decides such questions. An earlier case, _Dillon v. Gloss_, had said amendments should be ratified within a “reasonable time.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment ratified in 1992, about two centuries after James Madison proposed it.

tossups.p: In 2017, the University of Texas changed a grade from a C to an A, decades after a student’s paper about this amendment launched the campaign that got it ratified. That student, Gregory Watson, had written to lawmakers in state after state.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment, ratified in 1992, that delays changes in congressional pay.

tossups.p: Ratified more than twenty years after the amendment that lowered the voting age to 18, this amendment was the only one added to the Constitution in the 1990s. Its idea had first been proposed in 1789.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment that stops a congressional pay raise from taking effect until after the next House election.

tossups.p: Called “Article the Second” in the list Congress sent to the states in 1789, this amendment came right after a proposal about how many people each House member should represent, which has never been ratified.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this amendment about congressional pay, which finally became part of the Constitution in 1992.

tossups.p: Public anger over Congress raising its own pay in the 1980s helped push dozens of state legislatures to approve this amendment, which had sat unratified for nearly two centuries. In May 1992, it reached the 38 states needed for ratification.
tossups.r: It delays congressional pay changes until after a House election. For 10 points, name this amendment first proposed by James Madison.

tossups.p: Article I of the Constitution says members of Congress shall be paid an amount “to be ascertained by law,” which means Congress sets its own salaries. The First Congress paid its members six dollars for each day they attended.
tossups.r: James Madison proposed this amendment so that a pay change would have to wait until after the next House election. For 10 points, name this amendment ratified in 1992.

tossups.p: This amendment was one of two proposals from 1789 that were left out when ten others became the Bill of Rights in 1791. Only a handful of states had approved it by then, and it was nearly forgotten for decades.
tossups.r: It was finally ratified in 1992. For 10 points, name this amendment about congressional pay.

tossups.p: Federal courts ruled that the automatic yearly cost-of-living increases for members of Congress, set up by a 1989 ethics law, do not violate this amendment, which was ratified just a few years after that law passed.
tossups.r: It delays any other change in congressional pay until after the next House election. For 10 points, name this amendment, finally ratified after about 202 years.

trap.title: Get the number right
trap.body: The last few amendments blur together. The 26th Amendment (1971) lowered the voting age to 18, the 25th covers what happens if a president dies or cannot serve, the 22nd limits presidents to two terms, and the 20th moved Inauguration Day to January. Some players also say “Bill of Rights,” because this amendment was proposed in 1789 along with the first ten, but it was not ratified until 1992.
trap.fix: Congressional pay, Gregory Watson, a C on a college paper, 1992, and 202 years all mean the Twenty-seventh Amendment. Say the number clearly. Voting age 18 means the 26th, and two-term limits mean the 22nd.
trap.line: Real answer line: Twenty-seventh Amendment (or 27th Amendment or Amendment XXVII; do not accept other numbers)
